A_target.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be [[Definition:Banach Space|Banach spaces]] and $T: X \to Y$ a [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] [[Definition:Bounded Linear Transformation|bounded linear transformation]].
Then $T$ is an [[Definition:Open Mapping|open mapping]].

B_source.statement: A [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete metric space]] is not a [[Definition:Countable Union|countable union]] of [[Definition:Nowhere Dense|nowhere dense]] sets.

substitutions.the countable union: the closures of the images of the balls of radius n

derived.a set with non-empty interior: a ball around 0 inside the closure of T(B_1)

object_map.reformulation: Reduce openness to showing that the image of the unit ball contains a ball, first up to closure via Baire, then exactly via successive approximation.

validity_conditions: Surjectivity is needed for the images of the balls to cover Y.
Completeness of Y is used in the Baire step, and completeness of X to sum the approximating series.
proof_plan:
Let $B_r$ denote the open ball of radius $r$ about $0$ in $X$.
As $T$ is surjective, $Y = \displaystyle \bigcup_n \overline {\map T {B_n} }$.
By the [[Baire Category Theorem]], some $\overline {\map T {B_n} }$ has non-empty interior.
By linearity and symmetry, $\overline {\map T {B_1} }$ contains a ball $\map {B_Y} {0, r}$.

Let $
orm y < r$.
Choose $x_1 \in B_1$ with $
orm {y - T x_1} < \dfrac r 2$, then $x_2 \in B_{1 / 2}$ with $
orm {y - T x_1 - T x_2} < \dfrac r 4$, and so on.

As $\displaystyle \sum_k \norm {x_k} < 2$ and $X$ is complete, $x = \displaystyle \sum_k x_k$ exists with $\norm x < 2$ and $T x = y$.
Hence $\map T {B_2} \supseteq \map {B_Y} {0, r}$.
